methodology.score_meaning: Raw automated detector matches divided by evaluated attempts, including unsupported checks; not confirmed successful attacks or a measure of security or exposure. Legacy exposed_pct fields contain detector match rates only.
methodology.limitations: Web and HTTP connectors send only the last user message; prompt-leak assessment is unsupported because the synthetic system prompt is not sent. Provider API mode carries the full conversation, supporting synthetic prompt-leak tests, but does not verify disclosure of a deployed application's own instructions. Findings require review. File uploads, tool execution and authorisation boundaries are not independently verified.

categories.name: Hijacking
categories.description: A user hid an instruction inside text your AI was meant to process, not obey. When this succeeds, the model follows the hidden instruction instead of the task it was given.
categories.assessment_note: The connector supports this assessment. Automated matches require review.
categories.recommendation: Separate user-supplied content from instructions using explicit delimiters, and add a system-prompt rule that content inside those delimiters is data only and can never issue new instructions. Re-run this test after the change.

categories.name: Jailbreak
categories.description: A user asked your model to roleplay as an unrestricted version of itself. When this succeeds, whatever behaviour rules you think you've set were talked around.
categories.assessment_note: The connector supports this assessment. Automated matches require review.
categories.recommendation: Add an explicit instruction-hierarchy statement to your system prompt: user messages can never redefine the assistant's identity or permissions. Pair with an output check that flags any response claiming a new persona.
